reason: Terminated by Executive Order 9894, signed September 23, 1947, which orders that the San Clemente Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, established by Executive Order 7747 as amended by Executive Orders 8536 and 9787, be and is hereby discontinued. It states no delayed effective date, so the effective date is the signing date, 1947-09-23 (the order was published September 25, 1947, the alternative reading). Executive Order 9787 restated Executive Order 7747 to read as follows: it established the defensive sea area, barred vessels from navigating within it except as authorized by the Secretary of the Navy, and set the penalties provided by law for violations. All three provisions depend on the existence of the area and ended when the area was discontinued.

Terminated by Executive Order 12292 (signed February 23, 1981), section 10(b) of which revokes Executive Order 9799 of November 8, 1946. Section 11 of Executive Order 12292 states that it is effective as of February 15, 1981, which is therefore the effective date of the revocation; the alternative reading is that the revocation operated from signing on 1981-02-23 or publication on 1981-02-25. February 15, 1981 is also the date the Foreign Service Act of 1980 took effect (section 2403(a)), repealing the 1946 Act whose section 411 power the order delegated; section 2401(a) of the 1980 Act continued orders issued under the 1946 Act until revoked or superseded, so the repeal by itself did not end the order and the express revocation is the end. The order authorized and directed the Secretary of State to exercise the President's power under section 411 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 to classify chief-of-mission positions into four classes, effective November 13, 1946. The label EO 9452 attached to one acting record in the dossier is the Federal Register issue holding Executive Order 12292, not an earlier revoking order.

Terminated by Executive Order 10011, signed October 22, 1948 (published October 26, 1948), paragraph 3(b) of which orders that Executive Order 9870 of July 8, 1947, and Executive Order 9982 of July 29, 1948, are hereby revoked. The order states no delayed effective date, so the effective date is the signing date, 1948-10-22. Executive Order 9982 extended and continued the provisions of Executive Order 9870 (foreign service allowances and allotments) to and including June 30, 1949, effective as of July 1, 1948. That own-terms end date (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end the extension when July 1, 1949 begins) was not reached because the express revocation came first. The proviso in paragraph 3(b) keeps rules and regulations prescribed under the revoked orders in effect until superseded under paragraph 3(a); it does not extend the revoked order itself.
